title: You Have Worked
text:
You have worked

twenty years


to gather

twenty million pesos


but we

would give twenty million pesos


not to work

as you have worked
editorial_note: The translation keeps the poem's blunt reversal of money earned into money one would pay to avoid such labor.

title: I Have Been Very Ardent
text:
I have been very ardent.

The story of my life has been a love story.

Of love? Of loneliness!

Of loneliness and love.

Of loneliness.

Sexually

very ardent.
editorial_note: The translation preserves Cardenal's self-correction from love to loneliness and back to desire.

title: You Enter Again Like Music, Like Light
text:
You enter again like music, like light,

music without acoustic waves, light without photons.

Caress without touch, only the pure caress.

The one who invented sex

will he not know how to love?
editorial_note: The translation keeps the poem's physical metaphors made immaterial before the final theological question.

title: Perhaps We Will Marry
text:
Perhaps we will marry

this year


my love, and

have a little

house


And perhaps

my book will be published,


Or the two of us will go

abroad


Perhaps Somoza will fall

my love
editorial_note: The translation preserves the poem's mingling of domestic hopes, literary hopes, exile, and revolution.

title: If When It Was
text:
If when it was

the April rebellion


they had killed me

with them


I would not have met you


and if now

it had been

the April rebellion


they would have

killed me with them
editorial_note: The translation follows the poem's conditional logic between survival, love, and revolutionary death.
